newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says inflation may be lower than forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says inflation may be lower than forecast.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Bernie Fraser said on Thursday he agreed with the government's forecasts for economic growth but thought inflation could be lower.
Fraser said also in a submission to a parliamentary committee that the effects of the last reduction in interest rates on July 31 would only become apparent in the months ahead.
"The budget forecast for 1996/97 envisage a sixth year of growth of around 3.5 percent, with inflation of about 2.75 percent," Fraser said.
"We agree generally with these forecasts, but we think inflation through 1996/97 could turn out to be a little lower," he said.
The budget forecast the consumer price index (CPI) to rise 2.0 percent in year average terms in the year to June 30, 1997 and for underlying inflation to rise 2.75 percent.

"The growth foreasts are underpinned by a reasonably encouraging outlook for our major trading partners, good levels of business and consumer confidence and the absence of any major 'imbalances' in the domestic economy," Fraser said.
He said the further 14 percent rise expected in business investment in 1996/97 is an important key to achieving the growth forecast.
Fraser repeated that the bank was confident inflation in the Setpember quarter would be comfortably within the two to three percent target range, and that it would remain there over the year ahead.
